Benchmarks for Generated Code
Anonymous
Abstract
We describe benchmarks that evaluate code written by language models.

1

Background

AlphaSuite measures the functional correctness of programs generated from
comments, and sampling 50 programs per problem solves 61.5% of its problems [1]. BetaBench contains prompts for 300 coding
tasks that span nine programming models [2]. GammaEval evaluates whether language models can write vector kernels that are both correct and
faster than a reference library [3]. On a suite of 180 library workloads, current
models match the reference library in fewer than 15% of cases [2].

References
[1] Ann Author, Ben Author, and Cleo Writer. Measuring programs generated from comments. 2021.
[2] Jane Doe, Richard Roe, and Edgar Poe.
Can language models write code for many programming models?
In Proceedings of the Example Symposium on Software, pages 1-14. Example Press, 2024. doi: 10.5555/beta.2024. URL
https://doi.org/10.5555/beta.2024.
[3] Dana Coder and Eli Tester. GammaEval: Can language models write fast vector kernels? 2025. URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2901.00013.
